description: Mellea is a library for writing generative programs.

summary.one_liner: Mellea is a Python library for writing "generative programs," turning typed functions and Pydantic schemas into structured, validated LLM calls with automatic retries.
summary.what_it_does: The library lets you define an LLM call as a typed Python function using the @generative decorator, where the docstring serves as the prompt and the return type hint as the output schema. Pydantic schemas are enforced at generation time. You can attach natural-language requirements to any call, and Mellea validates the output and retries automatically. It also supports sampling strategies such as rejection sampling and majority voting, switchable with a single parameter change. Backends named in the README include Ollama, OpenAI, HuggingFace, WatsonX, LiteLLM, and Bedrock. It offers a mify helper for dropping Mellea into existing codebases and can expose generative programs as MCP tools.
use_cases: Extracting structured data from unstructured text into typed objects
Adding validation and automatic retries to LLM outputs
Building testable AI pipelines instead of brittle prompts
Choosing the best of multiple LLM generations
Integrating LLM calls into an existing Python codebase
Exposing generative functions as MCP tools
notable: @generative decorator: docstrings become prompts and type hints become enforced schemas
Requirements attached to calls with automatic validation and repair
Swappable sampling strategies such as rejection sampling and majority voting
mify helper for integrating into legacy code
